scholarships.title: Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship / TSH Changemaker Scholarship (Erasmus MC)

existing.funding_period: one-time award for one academic year
existing.description: You are applying for one of the following full-time Research Master’s programs at Erasmus University Medical Center: Health Sciences , Neuroscience , or Molecular Medicine .
eligibility: Applying for a full-time Research Master's programme at Erasmus MC: Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine
An excellent student by the faculty's standard, with an average grade equivalent to the Dutch grade of 8.0 on the Dutch 1-10 scale

Belong to one or more disadvantaged or underrepresented groups (limited financial, educational, social or health resources; refugee or newcomer status; ethnic or religious marginalisation; physical or mental disability; first-generation student; LGBTQI+ identity with potential safety risks; reduced social capital or sense of security)
Demonstrate community involvement, social contribution and commitment to engaging with the Changemaker alumni network
Nationality: EEA as stated on the Erasmus MC page
Unconditionally admitted to the master at the start of the programme, per the university-level description of this combined award
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants for a full-time Research Master's programme at Erasmus MC (Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine) who have a bachelor average equivalent to Dutch 8.0, belong to one or more disadvantaged or underrepresented groups, and demonstrate community involvement and commitment to the Changemaker alumni network. The Erasmus MC page states the nationality condition as EEA.
benefits: EUR 9,895 for costs of living and the statutory tuition fee for one academic year
Trustfonds component includes a monthly living allowance of EUR 600
One year of housing in a Social Hub Residence through the TSH Changemaker Scholarship
Partial tuition fee waiver for non-EU/EEA institutional-fee payers, where applicable
Mentorship, training and membership of a lifelong Changemaker alumni network
coverage: Living costs (Trustfonds component includes a monthly living allowance of EUR 600)
One year of housing in a Social Hub Residence (TSH Changemaker component)
Partial tuition fee waiver for non-EU/EEA institutional-fee payers, where applicable
requirements: Apply for one of the three eligible Research Master's programmes at Erasmus MC
Submit all documents as PDF using the naming format studentnumber_lastname_name of document_name of scholarship
Use only the provided EUR budget plan template
Upload a separate motivation letter for each scholarship if applying for more than one
Complete the application through the OSIRIS Cases portal
documents: Grade list in PDF format, covering only the highest degree
Budget plan in PDF format, using only the EUR budget plan template provided
Motivation letter in PDF format addressing the five questions the page lists
existing.english_requirement: The funded programmes are full-time English-taught Research Master's programmes at Erasmus University Medical Center; no separate VU-style English test score is specified on this page.
application_method: Apply for the Research Master's programme at Erasmus MC
Prepare CV, grade list, budget plan and motivation letter as PDFs
Log in to the OSIRIS student site, open Cases, and complete the scholarship application
existing.selection_notes: Because the number of scholarships is limited, Erasmus MC states that not every Research Master's programme can be funded and that the eligible programmes change each academic year. Awardees receive mentorship, training and access to a Changemaker alumni network.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving applicants to the Erasmus MC Research Master's programmes who belong to a disadvantaged or underrepresented group and can evidence community involvement.
existing.notes: The Erasmus MC page is school-specific and states 'Nationality: EEA'; the university-level page for the same combined award states that nationalities vary per school, so non-EEA applicants must check their own faculty's rule. The EUR 9,895 is the Trustfonds component for costs of living and the statutory fee, with the TSH Changemaker Scholarship adding one year of housing in a Social Hub Residence, and non-EU/EEA institutional-fee payers receiving a partial tuition fee waiver from the school where applicable.
existing.application_period: Annual Erasmus MC cycle; the published 2026-2027 round closed on 1 April 2026 at 23:59 CET and the next round's date is not yet published
existing.program_type: Combined need- and merit-based Master's scholarship for underrepresented students at Erasmus MC, pairing an Erasmus Trustfonds grant with the TSH Changemaker Scholarship

eligibility: National of Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, the United Arab Emirates or Yemen
Have received an official letter of admission to a one-year Master's programme at Leiden University, or be enrolled in the second year of a two-year Master's programme at Leiden University
Demonstrate a strong motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue
Submit a complete application for admission to Leiden University before the deadline
existing.eligibility_summary: Nationals of Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, the United Arab Emirates or Yemen who have either received an official letter of admission to a one-year Master's programme at Leiden University, or are enrolled in the second year of a two-year Master's programme at Leiden University.
benefits: Leiden University housing fee covered, with the rent itself not covered
Small remaining amount paid to the student in monthly installments
Option to arrange housing via Leiden University with the request fee paid from the scholarship
Mentoring programme with personal and professional guidance
Access to the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation's network and platforms
coverage: Leiden University housing fee (the fee only, not the rent itself)
A small remaining amount paid to the student in monthly installments
requirements: Submit a complete application for admission to Leiden University before the scholarship deadline
Submit proof of sufficient funds for the visa/residence permit application
Be able to fund your own travel and housing costs and the remainder of your living costs
Follow the application procedure published by the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation
documents: Official letter of admission to a one-year Master's programme at Leiden University, or proof of enrolment in the second year of a two-year Master's programme
Proof of sufficient funds for the student visa/residence permit application
English language test result, which is a prerequisite of admission to Leiden University and paid for by the applicant
Scholarship application documents as specified by the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation
existing.english_requirement: An English test is a prerequisite of admission to Leiden University. The costs of the test must be covered by the applicant.
application_method: Apply for admission to a one-year Master's programme at Leiden University and submit a complete admission application before the deadline
Follow the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation's application requirements for this scholarship
Optionally request housing via Leiden University, whose housing request fee is paid directly from the scholarship
existing.selection_notes: The fund was established through a partnership between the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund in 2018. It provides one scholarship annually to a Master's student from an Arab country to attend a Master's programme at Leiden University, on the basis of exceptional academic excellence and motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. A separate variant fund, the LUF - Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund: Extra Gaza Scholarship, exists for Gazan students and should not be confused with this award.
existing.best_fit: A high-achieving applicant from one of the listed Arab countries who already holds a Leiden admission letter for a one-year Master's programme, or is entering year two of a two-year Leiden Master's, and can evidence a commitment to Euro-Arab dialogue.
existing.notes: Leiden University states explicitly that this is not a full scholarship: 'This is not a full scholarship and does not cover all the recipients expenses in The Netherlands.' It does not apply to LLM Advanced Studies programmes, which have higher tuition fees. Housing can be arranged via Leiden University and the housing request fee is paid from the scholarship, but the rent itself is not covered. The fund is also described as strengthened by a mentoring programme offering personal and professional guidance and access to the Foundation's network and platforms.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle: applications open 1 January and close 31 March at 23:59 CET each year
existing.deadline_display: 31 March 23:59 CET annually (applications open 1 January annually)
existing.program_type: Named scholarship fund for exceptional students from the Arab region, administered by Leiden University in partnership with the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation
